sectionsUsed: Chapter 11 Indexes: indexes enhance performance and add overhead (model)

11.1 Introduction: without an index the system must scan the entire table; the index is kept synchronized, adding overhead to data manipulation; unused indexes should be removed; the planner uses an index when cheaper than a sequential scan (activities 1, 2, 4; recap)
11.2.1 B-Tree: the default index type; equality and range operators and sorted output (model, activity 2)

11.3 Multicolumn Indexes: most efficient with constraints on the leading (leftmost) columns; equality constraints on leading columns plus an inequality on the first column without equality limit the scanned portion (activity 2 teaching, editor analysis, hints)
CREATE INDEX Synopsis and Description: optional name, USING method default btree, column list (activity 2 editor subset)
Default name chosen from the table and columns; confirmed on PostgreSQL 17.5 as orders_customer_id_id_idx-style naming (editor output)
5.5.3 Unique Constraints and 5.5.4 Primary Keys: automatically create a unique B-tree index (activity 3)
5.5.5 Foreign Keys: a foreign key does not automatically create an index on the referencing columns (activity 3)
